designation: IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Nagaland, supervised by the Gauhati High Court — Kohima Bench. Following the 2021–2022 reorganisations, Nagaland has 17 districts (Tseminyu, Niuland, Chümoukedima, Shamator newly carved out). English is the State and judicial working language under the Nagaland Official Language Act, 1967. Article 371A and the Nagaland customary law framework heavily influence civil and family jurisdiction — Village Courts, Area Councils and Customary Courts under the Nagaland Village and Tribal Councils Act, 1978 operate parallel to regular courts in respect of Naga customary matters.

party_designation.state: State of Nagaland through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Nagaland, Kohima

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly verify and declare that the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ of the above petition are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are based on information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: English is the sole official language of pleadings before the subordinate judiciary in Nagaland.
Bail applications under S.483 BNSS (formerly S.439 CrPC) must disclose prior rejections and be accompanied by certified copy of the FIR.
Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) require certified copy of FIR and grounds; Gauhati HC Kohima Bench is the preferred forum for serious offences.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the Gauhati High Court Rules with requisite court-fee stamp.
Court-fee under the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as adopted by Nagaland.
SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, POCSO and NDPS cases tried by designated Special Courts at the district headquarters.

Article 371A protects Naga customary law and procedure — no Act of Parliament in respect of religious or social practices, customary law and procedure, administration of civil and criminal justice involving decisions according to Naga customary law, ownership and transfer of land applies unless the State Legislative Assembly so decides. Customary courts (Village Court, Area Council Court, Dobashi Court) under the Nagaland Village and Tribal Councils Act, 1978 and Rules thereunder retain primary jurisdiction over Naga customary matters; advocate must verify forum jurisdiction (customary court vs. regular sessions/district court) before filing — particularly in matters involving land, inheritance, marriage and family disputes among Nagas.
e_filing_note: e-Filing operational at Kohima, Dimapur via eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide.
